title: One Cell or Many
description: Some living things are a single cell; others have trillions. Learn the difference to outwit Necrosis and free piece 3.

content.value: Some organisms are made of just ONE cell. They are called UNICELLULAR organisms. That single cell does everything needed for life — moving, eating, growing and reproducing. Examples include Amoeba, Paramecium, and bacteria.

UNICELLULAR (one cell)      MULTICELLULAR (many cells)
🦠  Amoeba                   🌳  Trees
🦠  Paramecium              🐕  Animals
🦠  Bacteria                🧑  Humans

Organisms made of MANY cells are called MULTICELLULAR. Plants, animals and humans are all multicellular. In these organisms, different groups of cells do different jobs — muscle cells contract, nerve cells carry signals, and so on. This 'division of labour' lets big organisms work efficiently.
Amoeba: A Cell That Changes Shape

The Amoeba is a famous unicellular organism with no fixed shape. It pushes out finger-like extensions to move and to surround and swallow its food. Despite being a single cell, it is completely alive.
'Uni' means one and 'multi' means many. Unicellular = one cell; multicellular = many cells. A human body has trillions of cells!

Key Takeaway: Unicellular organisms (like Amoeba, Paramecium, bacteria) are made of a single cell that does everything. Multicellular organisms (plants, animals, humans) are made of many cells that share the work.

quiz.question: An organism made of a single cell is called…
quiz.explain: 'Uni' means one, so a single-celled organism is unicellular — like Amoeba.

quiz.question: Which of these is a unicellular organism?
quiz.explain: Amoeba is made of just one cell. Trees and dogs are multicellular.

quiz.question: In multicellular organisms, different cells…
options: all do exactly the same thing
quiz.explain: Different groups of cells specialise in different tasks, which is called division of labour.
